correctness.rationale: The exact primary source updates only edges |x_i-x_j|<c and includes each vertex’s own opinion. Initially 0-1 has gap a*c<c and 1-2 has gap (b-a)c>c for 0<a<1 and (3+a)/2<b<2. Only 0-1 repulsion acts, and direct shifted-neighbor averages give ((a-1)c/2,(a+1)c/2,bc). Its repulsive gap is exactly c and attractive gap is (b-(a+1)/2)c>c; both edges then inactive, hence frozen. Its diameter is c(b+(1-a)/2)>2c while initial bc<2c, excess c(b-(3+a)/2). At a=1/4,b=7/4,c=1 the exact fractions and 17/8>2 follow; sup c/2 is approached, not attained. Independent rational one-step recomputation and source eq (3.1)-(3.2) inspection corroborate. Original Prop 4.1 covers the 2-agent bound, implying sharp graph size. This does NOT contradict source’s separate convergence conjecture.

originality.rationale: Direct full-text inspection of the originating 2023 paper confirms the mixed-sign diameter inequality is explicitly a conjectural unsupported Theorem 4.11, not already known false or proved; the exact 3-node connected witness defeats its bound but converges. Prior public same-model one-antagonistic-edge equilibrium result classifies fully receptive states only, whereas witness becomes completely nonreceptive. Related signed opinion updates are distinct. No covering earlier explicit witness found in the searches, with unindexed priority risk.
residual_risks: Other researchers may already have publicly noted this elementary 3-agent counterexample to the 2023 proposed bound; no absolute originality certification.
A condition requiring initially receptive connectivity would be a different conjecture; the third vertex here is initially nonreceptive.
Strict inequality |gap|<c is essential to one-step freezing, not a statement for <=c conventions.
The claimed c/2 supremum is only within the exhibited open family, not a global all-network maximum.
